properties.identity: triangulene (C22H12), triplet state S=1, multiplicity 3 — ground state
properties.ground_state: triplet (S=1, M=3), two unpaired pi electrons
properties.singlet_triplet_gap_uncertainty_kcal_mol: about +/-3 (multireference spread 10.6-16.2 kcal/mol: MR-CISD+Q 13.0, MR-CISD 17.7, CASPT2/NEVPT2 J=10.6, MR-CISD+Q sigma+pi 16.2)
properties.singlet_triplet_gap_level_of_theory: literature-benchmarked value, MR-CISD+Q/6-311G(2d), pi-CAS(4,7), vertical 1 3A2' -> 1 1E' (Das, Muller, Plasser, Lischka, J. Phys. Chem. A 120, 1625 (2016), Table 1; the current secondary literature quotes 13-16 kcal/mol)
properties.singlet_triplet_gap_note: This gap describes the open-shell (diradical) singlet, which NO permitted method here (xtb, pm7) can represent. Our own calculations cannot resolve it; they can only bound it. The declared value is therefore the accepted multireference/experimental-benchmarked number, not a value computed in this project.
properties.pm7_closed_shell_singlet_upper_bound_def: The PM7 adiabatic separation E(M=1 restricted closed-shell) - E(M=3 UHF) is documented, with its numbers, in work/calc/REPORT.md and PROCESS.md; it is an UPPER BOUND for the closed-shell Kekule/quinoidal singlet and is NOT the singlet-triplet gap.
properties.method: Gaussian 16, PM7, UHF (auto-selected for M=3), route '#p opt freq PM7 guess=mix'
properties.smiles_note: the plain (non-Kekule diradical) SMILES mandated by the task is used as the node identity; RDKit perception of the optimized geometry writes the charge-separated closed-shell form [H]c1c([H])c2c([H])c3c([H])c([H])[c+]([H])c4c([H])c5c([H])c([H])c([H])c6c([H])c(c1[H])c2c(c34)[c-]65, which has an identical canonical heavy-atom graph (22 C, 27 C-C bonds, 6 rings, 12 H, planar to 0.0005 A) — a representation artefact, not a different species. Single entry kept so the node is unambiguously one molecule (not a multi-component species).
properties.computed_observations: No numerical energies are declared here because the workflow's geometry stage for this node is unresolved (harness identity check false negative, see smiles_note). All numbers from the native logs are documented in PROCESS.md and work/calc/REPORT.md and can be read directly from work/calc/PM7_T1.log (triplet, M=3) and work/calc/PM7_S1.log (M=1 reference).
properties.gfn2_xtb_counterevidence: GFN2-xTB places its restricted (--uhf 0) closed-shell solution below its --uhf 2 triplet at a geometry whose frontier gap is essentially zero (degenerate occupations) - a closed-shell artefact rather than a physical negative gap; numbers in work/calc/REPORT.md, native outputs work/calc/xtb/S1/GFN2_S1.out and work/calc/xtb/T1/GFN2_T1.out.

properties.identity: triangulene (C22H12), multiplicity 1: the lowest state a single-reference calculation can reach is the closed-shell Kekule/quinoidal singlet (S=0, M=1); the physical lowest singlet is an open-shell (diradical) 1 1E' state
properties.accessible_reason: The open-shell (diradical) singlet that defines the singlet-triplet gap is not accessible at the permitted level of theory: PM7 runs RHF for multiplicity 1 and GFN2-xTB has no broken-symmetry option (the method-policy parser rejects Gaussian UHF/UPM7/ROHF routes). The closed-shell RHF solution below IS a genuine 0-imaginary-frequency minimum and is delivered as the restricted singlet reference, but its energy is only an upper bound for the closed-shell state, 46.84 kcal/mol above the triplet at PM7.
properties.smiles_note: the plain (non-Kekule diradical) SMILES mandated by the task is used as the node identity; RDKit perception of the optimized geometry writes the charge-separated closed-shell form [H]c1c([H])c2c([H])c3c([H])c([H])[c+]([H])c4c([H])c5c([H])c([H])c([H])c6c([H])c(c1[H])c2c(c34)[c-]65, which has an identical canonical heavy-atom graph (22 C, 27 C-C bonds, 6 rings, 12 H, planar to 0.0005 A) — a representation artefact, not a different species. Single entry kept so the node is unambiguously one molecule (not a multi-component species).
properties.computed_observations: Observed in the untouched native log work/calc/PM7_S1.log (Gaussian 16, PM7, restricted closed-shell RHF M=1, opt+freq, normal termination, 0 imaginary frequencies, lowest modes 73.88/77.10/102.66 cm^-1): E(RPM7) = 0.220288108854 Eh, ZPE correction 0.256477 Eh, HOMO-LUMO 3.22 eV, planar, C-C 1.3885-1.4358 A (modest Kekule/quinoidal alternation).

edges.channel: spin-state excitation: triplet (S=1) -> closed-shell singlet (S=0), same C22H12 framework, no bond reorganization, no saddle point / no IRC

dag_refs.note: node and edge ids equal the DAG delivery-target names so the artifact and the DAG refer to the same elements
